title: ChatGPT Plus vs Business vs Enterprise: which should your staff get?
description: Which ChatGPT plan to roll out at a 40-500 person firm: dated prices at 50 and 200 seats, data and admin controls, and who each plan fits.
topic: ChatGPT Plus vs Business vs Enterprise
job: choosing a ChatGPT plan for the team
verdict: Pick Business Standard, billed yearly, for most firms under 200 staff: same $20 a seat as Plus, with admin controls[^2][^3].
Pick Plus only for one person's own, non-confidential work; OpenAI may train on those chats unless they opt out[^1][^12].
Pick Enterprise if you need automatic offboarding, audit logs, a BAA (health-data contract) or over 200 seats[^2][^5].
Pick a monthly Business pilot first if use is unproven; firms leave 36% of software licences unused[^2][^32].
Pick neither until you check the AI chat already in your Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace plan[^36][^37].

summary: Plus, Business and Enterprise run near-identical ChatGPT; the plan decides who controls the account and data[^1][^2]. Plus belongs to one person, and OpenAI may train on those chats unless they opt out[^12]. Business gives the firm sign-in, admin and no training by default; Enterprise adds audit logs and retention control[^2][^11].

recipes.name: 1. Pilot in one unit: 8-15 staff for 60-90 days
recipes.when: You want proof in one unit or site before a firm-wide spend. Use Business billed monthly, not Plus, because pilot staff will still paste company data[^2][^12].
flow: Ops lead: pick two or three repeat tasks and 8-12 volunteers from two departments
IT: create the Business workspace, verify the email domain, turn on company sign-in (SSO) and two-step sign-in (MFA)
IT: choose which connected apps are switched on
Department head: name who checks AI output before it leaves the team
Ops lead: time each task before the pilot, so there is a before-and-after number
Ops lead: read weekly use in the admin analytics dashboard
Ops lead and finance: at day 60-90, move to yearly billing or stop
recipes.cost: 10 seats × $25 × 3 months = $750; 12 seats = $900, at list prices read 26 Nov 2026[^2][^5]. OpenAI's pages differ on the minimum seat count, so check at checkout[^5][^8].

recipes.name: 2. Whole-firm rollout, 40-200 staff
recipes.when: Your firm has no BAA or data-residency rule and stays under Business's 200-seat cap[^5][^6]. Buy Standard yearly for everyone who will use it, and Premium only for proven heavy users[^2][^5].
flow: Ops lead: write a one-page AI use policy: what data may go in, who reviews what
IT: set up SSO and a verified domain, and make auto-join need approval
IT: keep a manual offboarding checklist, since Business has no SCIM
IT: help staff with personal Plus accounts move or separate their history
Department heads: pick uses for each role and name a reviewer for each
Finance: set credit usage alerts if you buy extra credits
Ops lead: review seats each quarter and reassign idle ones
recipes.cost: Worked example, 120 staff billed yearly: 108 Standard and 12 Premium seats come to $40,320 a year[^2][^5]. All Standard, the same 120 seats cost $28,800 a year[^2].

recipes.name: 3. Regulated firm, or more than 200 staff
recipes.when: Pick this past 200 seats, because new Business workspaces stop there[^6]. Also pick it if you need a BAA, retention control, audit logs, data residency or automatic offboarding[^2][^5].
flow: Compliance or legal: list hard needs: BAA, retention period, residency, eDiscovery
Ops lead: get a written quote with seat minimum, included credits and true-up terms (charges for seats added mid-contract)
IT: connect SCIM to your identity system and set role-based access
IT and security: copy Compliance API logs to your archive; OpenAI keeps them 30 days
IT: plan the personal-account move; on Enterprise, staff get 7 days to choose
Department heads: keep sign-off rules for each role
recipes.cost: OpenAI publishes no Enterprise price[^2]. Third parties report about $60 a seat a month with a 150-seat minimum, about $108,000 a year at the floor[^23][^22].

humanRole: IT decides who gets in and who gets out. On Business, IT removes leavers by hand because there is no SCIM; Enterprise automates it[^8][^9][^10].
The ops lead and IT decide which company systems ChatGPT can read. Business admins choose which apps are on; on Enterprise, all apps start switched off[^18].

A named reviewer in each team, such as the controller for finance drafts, checks AI output before it leaves the firm. NIST advises checking sources and citations, and ChatGPT Work can pause for a person to approve key steps[^24][^15].
Licensed staff keep their professional duties, and compliance owns the record. Lawyers keep confidentiality duties, and FINRA says its supervision rules apply to AI[^25][^26][^19].

ownData.title: What does a year of ChatGPT cost at 50 and 200 seats?
ownData.intro: On 26 Nov 2026 we read OpenAI's pricing and help pages, then multiplied each monthly list price by 12 and by 50 or 200 seats[^1][^2][^3][^5]. OpenAI publishes no Enterprise price, so that row uses third-party reports[^23][^22]. At 50 staff, that reported floor costs about nine times Business Standard[^23][^2].
rows: Monthly only, no admin, may train on chats[^3][^12]
Same cash as Plus, with company controls[^2]
25% more for the right to stop any month[^2]
Enterprise at a reported $60 a seat
Reported, not an OpenAI price. Range $45-75 a seat a month[^23][^22].
ownData.note: Zavient price check, read 26 Nov 2026: US list prices before tax, which can vary by country[^5]. It leaves out extra usage credits, promotions and API spend[^17][^2]. Plus is shown for cost only, and 200 seats is the Business cap for new workspaces[^6].

example.input: Illustrative: a 90-person distributor where six staff expense personal Plus accounts. A buyer pastes a supplier's price list into a personal chat to draft a reorder email. The firm can't see or delete that chat, and training is on unless the buyer opted out[^12][^13].
example.output: After: those six and 30 more get Business Standard seats at the same $20 a month, billed yearly[^2]. IT verifies the domain and turns on SSO, and work chats stay in the company workspace with no training by default[^9][^11]. When the buyer leaves, IT removes the seat by hand and gives it to someone else[^9][^5].

watchOuts: Letting staff keep personal accounts: 32.3% of workplace ChatGPT use runs through them, and 57% of surveyed workers admit entering sensitive data[^27][^28]. Fix: buy a workspace and move people over with OpenAI's onboarding steps[^20].

Paying for seats nobody uses: firms leave 36% of software licences unused, and only 30% of one UK government Copilot pilot used it daily[^32][^35]. Fix: start monthly with volunteers, check admin analytics and reassign idle seats[^2][^5].

Leaving workspace defaults on: Business members can invite others, and each accepted invite is a paid seat[^8][^7]. Fix: an owner reviews pending invites, auto-join needs approval, and IT runs an offboarding checklist[^8][^9].

Assuming Business covers regulated data: self-serve Business offers no BAAs, Zero Data Retention or invoicing, and OpenAI points you to a contracted plan[^5]. Fix: if you need a BAA, residency or eDiscovery, price Enterprise from day one[^2].

Planning a Business rollout past 200 people: since 24 Aug 2026, new Business workspaces cap at 200 paid seats, and support can't raise it[^6][^8]. Fix: past about 150 staff, get an Enterprise quote before the workspace fills[^2].

Budgeting seats, not usage: from December, Plus and Business share one allowance across ChatGPT and Codex, and longer Work tasks use more[^16][^15]. Fix: set credit usage alerts, since 78% of IT leaders report surprise AI charges[^17][^33].

faq.q: Is ChatGPT Business worth it over Plus for a team?
faq.a: Yes, on yearly billing: a Standard seat costs $20 a month, the same as Plus[^2][^3]. It adds company sign-in, admin controls and no training on your data by default[^2][^12]. Billed monthly, it costs $25[^2].

faq.q: Can admins see employees' ChatGPT Business chats?
faq.a: Yes, plan as if they can. OpenAI's privacy page says Business admins can view, export and delete members' conversations[^11]. On Enterprise, compliance teams pull logs through the Compliance API[^19].

faq.q: Can we buy ChatGPT Business for just a few people?
faq.a: Yes, but OpenAI's pages differ on the minimum[^5][^8]. One help article says one paid seat starts a workspace; the pricing page says from two users[^5][^1]. Check at checkout.

faq.q: Is ChatGPT Team the same as ChatGPT Business?
faq.a: Yes. OpenAI renamed Team to Business on 29 Aug 2025, and existing contracts stayed in effect[^6].

faq.q: What is the difference between Chat and Work in ChatGPT?
faq.a: Chat answers questions and drafts short pieces; Work is an agent for multi-step tasks that end in a file you review[^14][^15]. Work runs on Plus, Business and Enterprise, and shares usage limits with Codex[^39][^21].

faq.q: How much does ChatGPT Enterprise cost?
faq.a: About $60 a seat a month with a 150-seat minimum, by third-party reports; OpenAI publishes no price and quotes each deal[^23][^22][^2]. Treat that as a planning number and get a written quote.

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy a ChatGPT plan when the job is everyday writing, research and analysis for many staff[^30]. Most enterprise AI is now bought: 76% of solutions in 2025, up from 53% in 2024[^30]. MIT found bought or partnered tools reached deployment about twice as often as internal builds[^29][^40].
buyVsBuild.build: Build when your own data or rules are the edge, such as one narrow workflow tied to your systems[^29]. A build runs on OpenAI's API (developer access), billed apart from ChatGPT; Business includes up to $500 a month in API credits, per OpenAI[^5][^2]. Gartner says at least half of GenAI projects were dropped after proof of concept, so start small[^31].

pickElse: You already pay for Microsoft 365: Copilot Chat comes at no extra cost on eligible plans[^36]. Microsoft 365 Copilot Business adds answers drawn from your email and files for $21 a user a month on top, billed yearly[^36].
You run Google Workspace: Business Standard, at $14 a user a month billed yearly, includes Gemini in Gmail, Docs and Meet[^37][^38]. Google says it doesn't train models on your company data[^37].

You need one narrow workflow, not a chat tool for everyone: a purpose-built tool or a small API build fits better[^29]. MIT found generic chat tools stall in critical workflows that need memory and customisation[^29].
Staff won't use it yet: fix the task list and training first[^35]. In one UK government pilot of 1,000 Copilot licences, only 30% used it daily[^34][^35].

offer.heading: Rolling ChatGPT out to your team?
offer.body: In 30 minutes we map your seat count, data rules and tools to a plan and a rollout. You leave with a year-one cost and the first workflow to pilot.

reviews.notes: Wants one pick to forward, a cost and a first step. Bottom line gives the pick by firm size; own-data table gives the yearly cost. The pilot had no before-and-after measure; added 'Ops lead: time each task before the pilot' to recipe 1. FAQ questions are real buyer questions, seen on r/ChatGPT (Aug and Oct 2025), r/OpenAI (Feb and May 2026), OpenAI's own Business FAQ, and the keyword list (chat vs work in chatgpt, 390 a month); Enterprise cost is the business vs enterprise search.

Reads on a phone. The Business vs Enterprise table ran 11 rows; cut the vendor-marketing Support row. Expanded jargon a non-IT reader would stall on: SSO and MFA in the pilot steps, true-up in the Enterprise quote step, and eDiscovery/DLP/SIEM as legal-hold and security tools. One own-data sentence ran 26 words; split and shortened.

Wants to know if one unit or site can pilot first and what it costs that unit. Renamed recipe 1 to 'Pilot in one unit' and said it gives proof in one unit or site before a firm-wide spend. Pilot cost ($750-$900) is in the recipe. No sourced figure exists for time saved, so none is claimed.

Read as the controller or ops lead whose team would use it most. Wants to know who checks output and whether regulated data is allowed. Made the reviewer bullet concrete (the controller for finance drafts). The 'Assuming Business covers regulated data' watch-out and the Enterprise table rows answer the rules question; ABA and FINRA lines cover licensed staff.

Steve, 60-150 staff, decides in 10 seconds: the title and first bullet answer him (Business, yearly, same $20 as Plus). He worries Enterprise is being upsold; added to the own-data intro that a reported Enterprise floor costs about nine times Business Standard at 50 staff, labelled as reported. The Copilot alternative now says the $21 is on top of an eligible Microsoft 365 plan, so he doesn't compare it to $20 unfairly. Offer says what he leaves with: a plan, a year-one cost and a first pilot.

answers.recipes: Business Standard, billed yearly, fits most firms under 200 staff; Plus suits one person, and Enterprise suits firms needing audit logs, a BAA or over 200 seats.[^2][^3][^5]
answers.human-role: Your IT team controls access and which systems ChatGPT can read, and a named reviewer checks AI output before it leaves the firm.[^8][^18][^24]
answers.example: ChatGPT itself works almost the same on all three plans; what changes is who controls the account, the data and the audit trail.[^1][^2]
answers.what-goes-wrong: Teams most often leave staff on personal accounts, pay for seats nobody uses, and keep risky workspace defaults on.[^27][^32][^8]
answers.something-else: Pick neither if your Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace plan already includes AI chat, or you need one narrow workflow rather than chat for everyone.[^36][^37][^29]
answers.table-1: Plus is $20 a month on a personal account; Business Standard is $20-25 a seat with company admin; Enterprise has no public price and adds audit-log feeds.[^3][^12][^2][^5][^10] Business Premium seats cost $100-125 a month, and third parties report Enterprise at about $60 a seat.[^2][^5][^23]
answers.own-data: Business Standard billed yearly costs $12,000 a year at 50 seats and $48,000 at 200, the same cash as Plus.[^2][^3] Enterprise at a reported $60 a seat runs $108,000 at its 150-seat floor and $144,000 at 200.[^23][^22]
